items.headline: Morningstar/Dow Jones Oct 28: sterling fell to a 12-day low of $1.3269 in early European trade and 0.2% vs the euro to 0.8374 ahead of the Budget; 10Y gilt 5.354% (+1.2bp) — 'gilt markets are always a bit nervous heading into the autumn budget' (ING)

Reuters London morning Oct 28: sterling slips 0.1% to $1.329, a more than one-week low, and 0.1% vs the euro to 83.7p ahead of Healey's first Budget at 7:30am CT; 30Y gilt +2bp, having eased from its early-October high (highest since early 1998)
Reuters/QNA Oct 28: dollar flat at two-week high (DXY 102.40) into Super Wednesday; EUR/USD 1.1124, USD/JPY 157.945, USD/CAD 1.4063 ahead of the BoC; 10Y 5.01% (+2.2bp)

FXStreet Oct 28 preview: FOMC hold expected tonight (~10% hike prob), 2-3 dissents for a hike expected; BoC 25bp hike to 2.50% expected, its first since July 2023, with the MPR inflation forecast set for a substantial revision

Shekel gives back election-day gains, -1% to 3.084, as counted votes (~42%) confirm the Israel deadlock — Netanyahu bloc 57, opposition 47, Arab parties 16; double-envelope ballots Oct 29, official results Nov 4
items.source: Reuters Oct 28 Asia via breaking watch 00:32 CT — https://wncy.com/2026/10/27/dollar-holds-gains-ahead-of-fed-policy-signal-rbnz-decision/

items.headline: Reuters Asia: dollar at two-week high (DXY 102.40) ahead of Fed/BoC; EUR/USD flat 1.1129, GBP/USD flat 1.3307, USD/JPY 157.81; Fed funds futures price 91% for an FOMC hold

Oil rebounds in Asia: Brent +1.3% to $115.36, WTI +1.22% to $101.12 after Houthis claim a missile hit on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery (550k bpd) — Saudi authorities had not confirmed the strike (Reuters)

RBNZ SURPRISE HOLD at 2.75% in a 4-3 vote vs ~85-95% hike pricing — NZD fell as much as 1.7% to $0.5585 (Finnhub low 0.5580); all members agreed further tightening is likely, Breman raised restrictive territory, ANZ sees Dec/Feb/Mar hikes to 3.50%

Australia Q3 CPI hotter than the RBA's path: trimmed +1.0% q/q (Bank forecast 0.8%), Q3 trimmed 3.7% y/y, monthly Sep headline 4.3% y/y vs 4.2% exp — Nov 2-3 hike odds jumped to ~79-85%; AUD spiked to $0.7053
Bullock testimony: RBA will debate whether four hikes this year suffice to return inflation to target, at the Nov 2-3 meeting (Reuters Oct 28 Asia wire)
Super Wednesday preview: UK Budget 7:30am CT, BoC 8:45am CT (hike ~78-85%), FOMC 1pm CT (hold ~91%), Alphabet + Microsoft earnings after the close; KOSPI +6%+ in Asia on SK Hynix
BoJ trend inflation index jumped 3.2% y/y in September (from 2.6%), biggest since Oct 2023 — broadening price pressures cement the December BoJ hike case ahead of Friday's hold (Reuters)

US consumer confidence BEAT: 91.7 in October vs 81.2 fcst (Sep revised up to 84.2) — biggest beat since May 2025; present situation 120.4, expectations 72.6; Conference Board: recovery tracked easing gasoline prices, long-term downtrend intact
US new home sales BEAT: 676K SAAR in September vs 660K fcst (Aug 680K); inventory 476K, 8.4 months' supply, median $400,400 — demand steadier than feared
Dollar posts 1.5-week high (DXY +0.26%, third straight gain) into the FOMC on expectations Warsh delivers somewhat hawkish commentary; only 9% hike priced for this week, 91% for Dec 8-9 — Barchart

Scotiabank into FOMC: DXY 102.2 spot vs 100.5 fair value — sentiment support as rate differentials softened; only 3bp tightening priced for tomorrow, 22bp for December; a neutral hold leaves USD risks skewed lower

Treasury 5-year auction cleared at a lower yield than last month as demand recovers; 2Y ~4.733%, 10Y ~4.988% late US session (WSJ/Tradeweb) — yields off intraday lows, near Monday levels after the durable goods + confidence beats

US durable goods orders BEAT: +1.8% m/m in September ($345.4bn) vs 0.6% fcst (WSJ +1.7%); ex-transport +0.5%, nondefense cap goods ex-aircraft +0.5%; nondefense aircraft +28.4% led; August revised up to +0.1% from flat — Census advance report
ADP weekly employment eased to 16.75K (week ended Oct 10) from 18.5K — cooling but still positive into the FOMC; low-impact pulse

Reuters London morning: dollar nudged higher on euro, yen and pound Tuesday as traders brace for the central-bank barrage; EUR/USD 1.1154 (-0.17%), GBP/USD 1.3324 (-0.14%), USD/JPY 157.73 (+0.16%); ING: steadier AI sentiment lets markets reconnect with the hawkish-Fed + high-energy backdrop

Japan services PPI held at 3.7% y/y in September (inline) — price pressures steady into Friday's BoJ; Finance Minister Katayama warned Tuesday Tokyo stands ready to take decisive action in the currency market
France revenue-section vote moved to Nov 3 (was Oct 27, originally Oct 20) — 2,828 of 3,396 amendments still unexamined; the budget fight runs into Thursday's ECB with OAT-Bund ~167bp

FXEmpire morning: DXY near a one-week high ~102.04; EUR/USD broke below its triangle to 1.1168 (1.1150 next floor, 1.1192 resistance); GBP/USD slipped below its 1.3356 floor to 1.3333 ahead of Wednesday's Budget; CME Dec-hike odds ~73% (Monday)

Overnight pulse (10pm CT): DXY 102.04, EUR/USD 1.1174 (-0.39% day), GBP/USD 1.3341 (-0.28%), USD/JPY 157.69 (+0.55%), gold $4,019.80 (-0.46%), WTI $100.80 (-0.94%), US 10Y 4.99% — dollar marginally firmer into Tuesday Asia ahead of the central-bank week

Reuters Tuesday Asia: yen slips to 157.73 (-0.16%), eroding last week's haven gains on risk-on mood and a weaker euro ahead of the Fed/BoE/ECB/BoJ week; BoJ seen holding at 1.25% Friday with December hike odds slightly better than even; services PPI 3.7% inline

Dallas Fed manufacturing Oct 13.4 (vs 7.0 fcst, Sep 9.8) — headline beat, internals split: new orders 9.3 (vs 30.7 Sep), production 15.8, prices paid 55.3, future index 38.1; dollar firmed into the NY close on the oil/geopolitics bid rather than the survey alone

NY close: see markets.json — levels at the 3:00 PM CT close; dollar firmed on the day (DXY ~102.00) as oil eased (Brent settled $115.81, -0.8%; WTI $101.76, -1.5%) on Qatar-mediated de-escalation hopes while Houthi claims on Saudi pipeline/airport targets continued without Riyadh confirmation
items.source: Reuters via London markets wrap Oct 26 — oil ~$114.6 (-2%) on Qatari mediators in Tehran; STOXX 600 +0.4%

items.headline: Chicago Fed CFNAI Sep +0.07 (vs -0.10 fcst; Aug revised to -0.08 from -0.04) — MA3 +0.03, just above trend; low-impact print, no dollar reaction (DXY 101.67)
